environment.platform: macOS-15.8.1-arm64 (Apple M4 Max, 14 cores, shared with other jobs; 1-minute load averages are recorded per run)
environment.threads: 4 OpenMP/torch threads per evaluation; verification runs started with nice -n 10, one at a time

downloads_for_reading_only: dm_clrs-2.0.3-py3-none-any.whl (131 KB, PyPI) unpacked in the scratchpad to read the dm-clrs source (specs, encoders, decoders, processors, losses, evaluation, samplers, run.py); not installed and not used at run time
data: CLRS-30 v1.0.0 (storage.googleapis.com/dm-clrs/CLRS30_v1.0.0.tar.gz, 85,628,509 bytes, SHA-256 7743b2f1..., no separate data licence; the CLRS code is Apache-2.0). scripts/prepare_clrs.py converts it into 30 compressed npz files in suite/_lib/data/clrs (21 MB, git-ignored, never redistributed) and checks each against the content digests in catalog/clrs-data-lock.json. In this session the 30 files converted by the package's earlier session were copied in and `prepare_clrs.py --check` verified 30/30 against the lock.
unit_tests: 2026-10-11: $PY -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_clrs*.py' -> 25 tests OK in 22 s (tests/test_clrs.py: specs, metrics against transcribed dm-clrs formulas, prediction validation, source guard, payload decoding, upgrade records against the data lock, 30-id partition into upgraded and withdrawn tasks, prepared data and splits; tests/test_clrs_training.py: seed equals the reference processor, triplet messages equal the dense CLRS expression, network sizes equal EvoPrompting Table 3 for all 30 algorithms, step checkpointing gives the same loss and gradients, one training step for every algorithm, sandboxed scoring is deterministic, eight invalid candidates rejected, wall-clock limit enforced). The numpy-only tests run without torch or data (CI); the others skip when torch or the prepared files are missing.
verification: For every kept task the generated suite evaluator was run on the seed (initial_program.py) and on two invalid candidates (a processor returning the wrong shape, and a program importing os); a processor without message passing (relu(Linear([node_fts, hidden])), no edge embeddings) was scored with the same parameters as a discrimination check. Where that processor scored at least 0.90 the seed was also trained with training seeds 1 and 2 (saturation rule: keep only if the seed's margin over that processor exceeds two standard deviations of the seed's score over the three training seeds). Tasks were withdrawn when the seed failed or timed out, did not beat the processor without message passing, or failed the saturation rule, and when the evaluation budget used for every task (a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes on 4 CPU threads) could not afford a meaningful number of training steps (see withdraw).

evoprompting-bubble-sort.reason: Cannot be trained meaningfully within the evaluation budget used for every CLRS task (a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes on 4 CPU threads). Bubble sort's CLRS-30 trajectories have 121 hint steps at 16 nodes and 2017 at 64 nodes: predicting the 32 OOD test graphs alone took 251 s with the seed processor, and one Adam step (batch 32, backpropagation through all 121 steps with activation checkpointing) took 5.4 s, so a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes affords about 20 training steps (1% of EvoPrompting's 2000-step search), which cannot rank architectures.

evoprompting-strongly-connected-componen.reason: Cannot be trained meaningfully within the evaluation budget used for every CLRS task (a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes on 4 CPU threads): trajectories of up to 96 hint steps at 16 nodes (324 at 64) make one Adam step take 5.1 to 9.4 s and the OOD test prediction 39 to 86 s, so a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes affords about 40 training steps (2% of EvoPrompting's 2000-step search).

evoprompting-articulation-points.reason: Cannot be trained meaningfully within the evaluation budget used for every CLRS task (a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes on 4 CPU threads): trajectories of up to 73 hint steps at 16 nodes (404 at 64) with 13 hint probes make one Adam step take 3.1 to 6.0 s and the OOD test prediction 43 to 82 s, so a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes affords about 60 training steps (3% of EvoPrompting's 2000-step search). It is one of the three algorithms EvoPrompting searched on.

evoprompting-quickselect.reason: No usable signal within the CPU limits. Trajectories of up to 83 hint steps at 16 nodes (479 at 64) make one Adam step take about 2.9 s, so about 80 training steps fit a 6-minute evaluation; and the published OOD accuracies of all models on this one-of-64 output (EvoPrompting Table 3: 0.13 to 0.79%; Ibarz et al.: 0.47%) are below the 1.6% chance level, so differences between candidates would be sampling noise.

evoprompting-dag-shortest-paths.reason: Cannot be trained meaningfully within the evaluation budget used for every CLRS task (a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes on 4 CPU threads): trajectories of up to 49 hint steps with 11 hint probes need activation checkpointing to stay under the memory limit (4.9 GB peak without it) and then take 3.0 to 5.2 s per Adam step, so a seed evaluation of about 6 minutes affords about 80 training steps (4% of EvoPrompting's 2000-step search); the depth-first-search task at a similar budget did not rank the reference processor above a graph-blind one (see evoprompting-dfs).

evoprompting-dfs.reason: At the affordable budget the score does not measure what the paper measures. Trajectories of up to 48 hint steps make one Adam step take 2.4 to 3.4 s (with the activation checkpointing needed to stay under the memory limit; 3.5 GB peak without), so about 100 to 120 steps fit a 6-minute evaluation. Measured at 120 steps: the Triplet-GMPNN seed reaches an OOD test score of 0.125 (0.029 after one step; in-distribution validation 0.80), but a processor without message passing reaches 0.161, so the score ranks a graph-blind processor above the paper's reference architecture.

evoprompting-knuth-morris-pratt.reason: No usable signal at the affordable budget. Trajectories of up to 25 hint steps on 20-node strings with 10 hint probes need activation checkpointing (3.0 GB peak without) and take 1.7 to 2.8 s per Adam step, so about 150 steps fit a 6-minute evaluation. Measured at 150 steps (64 of the 2048 OOD test strings of 80 nodes): the Triplet-GMPNN seed reaches 0.875 in-distribution validation accuracy but an OOD test score of exactly 0.0, and a processor without message passing also scores 0.0, so the score cannot rank architectures (EvoPrompting Table 3 reports 8.9 to 19.5% after full GPU training).

evoprompting-quicksort.reason: At the affordable budget the score does not measure what the paper measures. Trajectories of up to 92 hint steps (512 at 64 nodes) make one Adam step take about 3.2 s with activation checkpointing, so about 100 steps fit a 6-minute evaluation. Measured at 100 steps: the Triplet-GMPNN seed reaches an OOD test score of 0.263, while a processor without message passing reaches 0.340, so the score ranks a graph-blind processor above the paper's reference architecture.

evoprompting-minimum.reason: At the task budget the score does not rank the paper's reference architecture above a graph-blind processor. Measured at 1200 steps (256 of the 2048 OOD test arrays of 64 nodes): the Triplet-GMPNN seed scores 0.715 OOD, while a processor without message passing scores 0.863; both reach 1.0 in-distribution validation accuracy.

evoprompting-naive-string-matcher.reason: No usable signal at the task budget. Measured at 900 steps (256 of the 2048 OOD test strings of 80 nodes): the Triplet-GMPNN seed reaches 1.0 in-distribution validation accuracy (20-node strings) but an OOD test score of exactly 0.0, below the 0.047 of a processor without message passing, so the score cannot rank architectures (EvoPrompting Table 3 reports 73.4 to 79.8% after full GPU training).

notes: Triage note verified: EvoPrompting's search fitness is the negative product of best validation error and model size after 2000 training steps (Section 3 and Section 4.2), searched on three CLRS algorithms only (articulation points, Graham scan, Kruskal's MST), while the numbers it reports are OOD test accuracies of five discovered models on all 30 algorithms (Appendix A.6, Table 3). The local score is the OOD test score itself.

Triage note verified: CLRS-30 v1.0.0 has 32 OOD test samples (64 nodes) per algorithm, multiplied by 32 for Kadane and by 64 for quickselect, minimum, binary search, the two string matchers and segments intersect (dm-clrs 2.0.3 samplers.CLRS30 and specs.CLRS_30_ALGS_SETTINGS; confirmed by the converted archive in catalog/clrs-data-lock.json).

Triage note verified: the CLRS-30 data carry no separate licence (the dm-clrs README and package metadata state Apache-2.0 for the code only); the derived files are generated locally and never redistributed.

The PyTorch network with the seed processor has exactly EvoPrompting's Table 3 baseline model size for all 30 algorithms (tests/test_clrs_training.py), which checks the spec-driven encoders and decoders, pred-as-input and permutation handling against the paper's implementation; the code was not numerically cross-checked against the JAX original.
Runs before 2026-10-11 16:56 used the earlier 870 s wall-clock limit; the score depends only on the step budget, so their scores are unaffected by the change to 1700 s.
